clues: This village sits in Ecuador, north of the big city of Quito. It lies very close to the line of the equator.
This place is so dry it earned a nickname. Folks call it Piurita, or little Piura, for its dry air.
Long ago, the Cara lands reached south to this village. It was the far south edge of all their land.
Its shoe trade uses parts of the maguey plant. That plant is found all through this dry area.
Its main square holds a church named for the Lord of the Tree. Next to it stands a second church, full of odd art.
